stances.claim: The David v SET ruling -- 9 justices concurring (including Peralta and Caguioa who had previously abstained on the natural-born issue), 3 dissenting, 3 taking no part -- definitively settles the previously contested plurality-vs-majority question about whether Grace Poe's natural-born citizenship was approved by a majority of the 15-member Court; the answer is now unambiguously yes.
stances.rhetorical_move: vote-count-as-definitive-resolution framing (9 confirmed concurrences resolve plurality critique)

stances.claim: The Leonen ponencia's reading-the-Constitution-as-a-whole approach properly effectuates the document's purpose by presuming foundlings are natural-born unless substantial proof otherwise -- because the contrary conclusion would create 'an inferior class of citizens who are made to suffer that inferiority through no fault of their own,' which the column endorses as a strong anti-discrimination application of social justice principles.

The David ruling's September 20 timing -- 'away from the noise of the 2016 election' -- protects the Court and those advocating social justice for foundlings from accusations of political partisanship; the well-settled doctrine that election laws should be interpreted liberally and doubts resolved in favor of voter choice can now be reaffirmed without electoral suspicion.

Some of the dissenters in these two cases are CJ's close friends, but their honest differences of opinion never affect mutual personal esteem -- because friendship is based on 'mutual respect for the free market of ideas, not on the excessive desire for conformity or on the eerie silence of the cemetery'; friends can disagree without being disagreeable, and can differ without being difficult.
stances.rhetorical_move: personal-coda on judicial collegiality (mutual respect across doctrinal lines)

notable_anecdotes: Justice Leonen described as 'the Benjamin of the high court' -- using the biblical Benjamin (youngest son) to characterize the junior-most justice penning a landmark ruling; CJ's signature epithet for Leonen, recurring across columns.

The Leonen quote preserved at length: 'Concluding that foundlings are not natural-born citizens is tantamount to telling our foundling citizens that they can never be of service to the country in the highest possible capacities... Concluding that foundlings are not natural-born citizens creates an inferior class of citizens who are made to suffer that inferiority through no fault of their own. If that is not discrimination, we do not know what is.' One of the most quoted ponencia excerpts in CJ's columns from this period.

The full vote-count narration: 9 concurring (named in order), 3 dissenting (named), 3 abstaining (named with reasons -- prior SET membership) -- making the column a definitive single-source roster of the Court's positions for archival purposes.

CJ's two prior-column self-references: 'Analyzing the SET decision' (11/29/15) and 'Comelec gravely abused discretion in Poe's case' (4/10/16) -- building a three-column arc on the Poe citizenship saga.

The 'eerie silence of the cemetery' metaphor for false consensus -- CJ's most memorable single-phrase defense of doctrinal disagreement, contrasting genuine intellectual respect with conformity-based pseudo-friendship.

The closing aphorism: 'friends can disagree without being disagreeable, and can differ without being difficult' -- a parallel-construction adage that distills the personal coda into transferable wisdom.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban summarizes the Supreme Court's 9-3 ruling (with 3 abstentions) on September 20, 2016, in David v Senate Electoral Tribunal, which held that Grace Poe, a foundling, is a natural-born citizen of the Philippines and therefore qualified for the Senate and any public office requiring natural-born status. The landmark decision, written by Justice Marvic M.V.F. Leonen -- 'the Benjamin of the high court' -- upheld the presumption that 'all foundlings found in the Philippines are born to at least either a Filipino father or a Filipino mother' because this presumption 'arises when the Constitution is read as a whole, so as to effectuate its purpose.' The Court emphatically held that concluding otherwise would create 'an inferior class of citizens who are made to suffer that inferiority through no fault of their own. If that is not discrimination, we do not know what is.' Concurring with Leonen were CJ Sereno and Justices Velasco, Peralta, Bersamin, Perez, Mendoza, Jardeleza, and Caguioa; dissenting were Justices Del Castillo, B. Reyes, and Perlas-Bernabe; taking no part (due to prior SET involvement) were Justices Carpio, Leonardo-De Castro, and Brion. The ponencia also held that Poe validly reacquired her natural-born citizenship under RA 9225 after her US naturalization. This ruling is separate from but consistent with Poe v Comelec (March 8, 2016, 9-6, Justice Perez ponente) which had earlier declared her qualified to run for President -- though that decision was criticized because two majority justices (Peralta and Caguioa) declined to vote on natural-born citizenship and instead invoked Comelec's grave abuse of discretion (since the Constitution vests the power to rule on presidential qualifications solely in the PET), leaving critics to claim natural-born status had only plurality support. David v SET definitively settles this contention with nine justices, including Peralta and Caguioa, voting natural-born. Fortunately the September 20 ruling came 'away from the noise of the 2016 election,' insulating the Court from accusations of political partisanship and reaffirming the well-settled doctrine that election laws should be interpreted liberally with doubts resolved in favor of voter choice -- consistent with CJ's December 6, 2015 column opining that even Rodrigo Duterte's threatened typo-based disqualification should yield to 'substantial justice, not literal interpretation.' CJ closes with a personal coda: some dissenters in these two cases are his close friends, but their honest differences of opinion never affect mutual esteem because their friendship is based on 'mutual respect for the free market of ideas, not on the excessive desire for conformity or on the eerie silence of the cemetery' -- friends can disagree without being disagreeable, and can differ without being difficult.
